title: German Arthroplasty Registry
summary:
Artificial joint replacement is one of the greatest achievements of modern medicine. It allows effective and long-term treatment of pain, functional limitations, and restricted mobility. Joint replacement surgery is now regarded as a standard operation, for which the public has high expectations. The success rate, measured as the lifespan of the implant, is reported by many studies to be 95% after 10 years in many studies.

The German Arthroplasty Registry (EPRD) aims to further improve the overall health care of patients with artificial hip and knee joints in Germany. In particular, the focus is on finding out more about the hip and knee arthroplasty survival, i.e. the time during which implants remain functional in the body until a replacement operation becomes necessary.

The EPRD is a joint project of doctors (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Orthopädie und Orthopädische Chirurgie e.V.), hospitals, health insurance providers (AOK-Bundesverband eGbR and vdek e.V.), and implant manufacturers (BVMed - Bundesverband Medizintechnologie e.V.). As a voluntary medical registry, it has been collecting data on hip and knee replacement procedures since 2012, systematically linking this with routine data and analysing the information with regard to the quality of the implants and medical treatment. This enables the EPRD to make reliable statements on the quality of care and identify potential for improvement. In total, more than three million documentations have already been submitted (as of Q2/2025).

The knowledge gained from the registry is made available to the professional public through regular analyses, publications, and presentations. Findings can then be incorporated directly into the reality of care, thereby increasing patient safety. Selected EPRD analysis results are presented in the annual reports and published in international journals. Participating hospitals and manufacturers also receive individual reports.
